sections.title: 22. Host contract · literal ownership
sections.summary: The contract sections a Mod must declare (`agent` / `inboxRoutes` in pack.json, `settlement` / `drive` in config.json), the ownership boundary between contract and host literals, the choice payload type, and the fail-closed loading rule.
sections.source: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (text before the 2026-10-31 condensation)

rules.text: The generic tooling (`src/playtest.rs`) hard-codes no event name / narrative prefix / summary key / entry payload / inbox field name / settlement switch / advancement threshold — it always reads the contract of the loaded Mod. The contract is mandatory: a missing section, a missing field, a wrong type or a non-positive integer fails loading (non-zero exit or `ok=false`); that is the deliberate fail-closed choice.
The `agent` section of `pack.json` has eight fields: entryEvent / choiceEvent / summaryEvent / endingPrefix / metaKey / rejectionPrefixes (at least one) / replayPrefix / defaultPayload.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (contract table, pre-migration)

rules.text: The `inboxRoutes` section of `pack.json`: reserved keys externalIdField / payloadField / extMarker plus `<kind>` → `{action, fields[, write]}` (zero kinds is legal).
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (contract table, pre-migration)

rules.text: The `settlement` section (in `<config.json>`): requireEvents / requireNoFailedSteps / requireEnding / requireInboxConsumed.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (contract table, pre-migration)

rules.text: The `drive` section (in `<config.json>`): maxSteps / stallLimit / stepsPerRequirement (positive integers).
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (contract table, pre-migration)

rules.text: `<config.json>` is the path declared by the `ygg:agent/config` entry in `pack.json` (`data/config.json` for the seed Mod).

Upgrading an old Mod means filling in the four sections (two in `pack.json`, two in `config.json`); `cargo run --example pack -- <mod dir>` validates their shape at pack time (only what is declared is validated).

Ownership boundary: event names / ending prefix / summary key / rejection and replay prefixes / inbox fields and routes / settlement switches / advancement thresholds belong to the contract and must be declared by the Mod; what the host may keep as literals is the run-directory file names, the coordination phase names running / closing / finalized, the decision-command timeout (`DECIDE_TIMEOUT`) and poll interval (`DECIDE_POLL_INTERVAL`), the three `--drive` modes, the five-file set (`pack.json` / `manifest.json` / `mod.lua` / `schemas/` / `data/`), and the kernel seams (`save` / `load` / `state`, and the reserved `ygg.choice_selected` route). Criterion: would this literal change with another Mod? If yes, it belongs to the contract.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (ownership boundary, pre-migration)

rules.text: Only applications bound to a specific Mod and the generator side may keep event-name / ending-prefix literals, and every such file declares "bound" or "generator-side" in its header: adventure.rs, clients/godot/rust/src/logic.rs, clients/godot/project/main.gd|session.gd, spike/godot/**, packages/client-web/src/{kernel,session,kernel-wasm}.ts and crates/ygg-wasm/smoke.mjs are bound to `packages/mods/test-adventure`; packages/pipeline/src/{prompt,types,pack}.ts and scripts-dev/mock-llm-stub.mjs are generator-side; the generic tooling of crates/ygg-sandbox|ygg-lint and the test fixtures under tests/ may not add literals, and `ygg.choice_selected` is the reserved event name checked by the kernel domain (the contract's `choiceEvent` must use it).
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (literal-ownership table, pre-migration)

rules.text: The payload of `ygg.choice_selected` must be a **JSON number** (`--payload '1'`); sending it as a string (`--payload '"1"'`) is rejected by the kernel domain as VALIDATION "option does not exist". Every other action's payload is a string. Menu selection is the **only** passing channel for the human-action gate — dispatching `proposal.accept` / `gate.approve` / `coordinate.submit` / `verify.submit` / `review.note` directly through `--event` is always refused (the receipt's first line is `[REJECTED:ACTION]`).

Runtime projection of `docs/design/host/serve.md` §3.7.6: never add a run-state write endpoint to serve; human gates remain CLI/daemon-ticketed. POST/DELETE `/api/roots` is only volatile observation configuration and must write no save, mod KV, run.json/coordination or directory; the zero-disk-write tests pin the boundary.
